subject: STR or LTR? Verify permission and model separate scenarios
preheader: Local rules, property restrictions, revenue evidence, and operating costs come first

marketSnapshot.headline: The same property can have different permitted-use and operating scenarios
marketSnapshot.body: Short-term and long-term rental assumptions should not be blended. Before modeling an STR scenario, verify current zoning, licensing, registration, HOA or condominium restrictions, lease limits, taxes, insurance, lender terms, and transferability with authoritative local sources. Then build revenue and cost assumptions from relevant property-specific evidence.

dealSpotter.headlineNumber: Build the STR case from relevant comps
dealSpotter.body: Use dated, comparable revenue and occupancy evidence and itemize management, cleaning, utilities, supplies, platform fees, maintenance, taxes, insurance, furniture, and reserves. A higher gross-revenue scenario does not establish higher net return or future performance.

dealSpotter.address: Educational scenario: permit or transfer uncertainty
dealSpotter.headlineNumber: Resolve legal operation before relying on STR revenue
dealSpotter.body: Confirm the current ordinance, property eligibility, permit status, transfer rules, enforcement, and HOA or building restrictions with authoritative sources and local professionals. Model long-term rent separately if that use is permitted; do not let an analyzer decide the legal question.

dealSpotter.address: Educational scenario: both uses appear possible
dealSpotter.body: Keep STR and LTR revenue, vacancy or occupancy, costs, management, financing, insurance, and compliance assumptions separate. Review the downside and operational workload for each scenario. The comparison is not a recommendation to choose either use.

blogFeature.title: Cash-on-cash vs IRR — what each modeled metric measures
blogFeature.excerpt: Cash-on-cash and IRR answer different modeled questions and both depend on the evidence and timing assumptions entered. Neither establishes the right rental strategy.

qa.question: Is an STR strategy viable for this property?
qa.answer: That is property- and date-specific. Verify current local law, zoning, licensing, HOA or condominium rules, taxes, insurance, lender requirements, and permit transferability with authoritative sources. Build revenue from relevant dated comps and itemize all operating and setup costs. Also model any permitted long-term use separately. TrueCap can compare entered scenarios, but it does not verify legal permission, forecast bookings, or recommend a strategy.
